summary: The code reading holds up. I read the diffs of #1014, #1040, #1041, #1059, #1015 and #1016 against the branch source and found no side effects on unrelated paths, and their land verdicts are sound. The #1013 section has two problems. First, the run instruction is wrong: it says the laptop has AAC, but v17.24's own tests/tests.js:193-205 says Linux Chrome has no AAC encoder. On the laptop the committed #1013 test would fail outright, because its positive control needs a real AAC encode. Since v17.24 a test like this must call `await needsAac()` at the top, and the chain was written on v17.23 and does not. That is the real collision with v17.24. Separately, tools/ship.sh:974-990 refuses any exporter.js change unless the AAC tests ran on the machine shipping it, so the chain can only ship from the Mac. Second, the timeout finding is real (`await dec.flush()` has no cap), but the report puts the hang in the wrong place. decodedAACPeak runs before the muxer is built and before any video frame is rendered (branch exporter.js:1401-1437), not after the render, and Cancel is not checked until line 1427. The proposed Promise.race fix works with the existing catch. The text-merge claim is plausible: the chain's tests.js hunks sit next to, but do not overlap, v17.24's hunks (66012 vs 66013). It names a `release/v17.24` branch, but v17.24 is on main as 05d06c53. The report also misses that none of the 7 commits bump the `?v=` cache-busters. Its explanation of why #1015/#1016 never passed is honestly labelled a guess. ChatGPT's own #1013 note shows the same port-8894 setup booted the app once and dropped a half-loaded boot, which fits an intermittent bootstrap failure better than broken code. The cause is still unproven.

summary: The measurements may well be honest. The arithmetic mostly adds up: 8192-6125=2067 MiB is 25%, and the five steps do sum to 3411. The Reverb and Squish code paths are described correctly. But the "1080x1920 kernel plates" claim is wrong for all three tests it names. :82443 uses 200x260 plates. :82649 allocates exactly one 1080x1920 array. :83769 renders on a 640x520 comp, not a 1080x1920 plate (its cold +218 MB fits 640x520 getImageData churn). The test that really sweeps 1080x1920 plates, :83717 (tree :84048), is never named. The step window ":80547 to :83259" does not even contain :83769. Calling Squish a "trigger, not a cause" is a guess presented as verified. Its roughly 2,600 fresh 480x480 renders, each with a 0.92 MB getImageData, line up with the report's own "1966 maps of exactly 1 MB" and its typed-array micro-test. The report never mentions the Mac's #1095 suspect, the queue 333 effects-browser sweep (v17.23 :63595, tree :63922). It also never says whether that test passed in its container (87 tests failed there). And its "dropped canvases +0 MB" micro-test does not test canvases that are kept alive after leaving the page, which is what #1095 blames. So H12 neither confirms nor refutes #1095. Option 1 (split at :47436) is safe for test proofs, but it moves the queue 333 sweep into the second Chrome. That test's own comment says it takes minutes when run cold.

summary: H11 is useful and mostly careful. Its main finding holds up: sleeping is not where the suite's time goes, so safe test edits give a modest cut, not a halving. Three things need fixing before a builder acts on it. (1) The 921 S3 proposal, as written, weakens the proof. The test catches a race that lasts a few milliseconds, and it only works if each pair's channels are checked the moment that pair's `opened` resolves. Batching with Promise.all and then running the unchanged checks moves the check to after the slowest pair in the batch has opened. (2) The Mac estimate for the 'every tile' test rests on a stale ~49 s. The same comment block records that the test went past 240 s in every phone pass on 21 Sep and took 261-279 s alone at 380px. So the saving on a real machine is far larger than 40 s, and the '8% on a Mac' total understates it. (3) The parallel-pass idea leaves out the strongest argument against it, which is already in tools/ship.sh:161-164: two headless suites on one machine flaked a timing test and cost a whole ship, and that is why spotcheck and ship refuse to run side by side. _cdp.py does pick its own free debug port and temp profile, and the two --progress and .out files are already separate, so there is no port or file clash. But it would also need: a two-value ship_phase, a new rule for how a red desktop pass stops the phone pass (today the phone pass never starts if desktop is red), a .suite-seconds reading that is not inflated by contention, and starts staggered so neither run's start-up reaper races the other's Chrome. Memory on the 7.7 GB WSL laptop, which now ships (the DESKTOP-HC64AE0 line in tools/.suite-seconds), is a real risk the report pins only on 'a Mac with less memory'. Line numbers have drifted by roughly 300 in tests.js in the v17.24 tree (for example 'every tile' is now at :63922, 921 S3 at :32657, 967 1 at :101723), but the content they point to matches.

claims.claim: 921 S3 forty pairings can run in 5 batches of 8 with Promise.all with every assertion unchanged, saving ~90 s
claims.evidence: tests/tests.js:32651-32675: the test guards a race of a few milliseconds ('at the moment `opened` resolves, all three channels must be open'). The readyState check runs synchronously right after `await rtcPair921()`, which resolves on Promise.all([h.opened, g.opened]) at :32576-32579. If the 8 pairings are awaited together and the checks at :32662-32672 then run unchanged, 7 of the 8 pairs are checked late, after the slowest pair has opened, which gives their bulk channel time to open. The 1-in-10 race this test exists to catch would then pass. The pairs share no state (each builds its own RtcLink at :32569-32570), so concurrency itself is fine.
claims.correction: Batching is only assertion-preserving if each pairing's channel check and bulk send run in that pairing's own continuation (rtcPair921().then(check)), so each check happens the moment that pair opens. Then prove it with a mutation that makes `opened` resolve on ctl alone, and check that the batched test still goes red.

But the same comment, :63928-63931, says the test passed 240 s and failed every phone pass on 21 Sep, and measured 261, 266 and 279 s alone at 380px. ~49 s is the stale 2 Sep figure. fx-thumbs.js already has a suite seam, `_sliceMs` (js/fx-thumbs.js:1174 and :1818). claims.evidence: Mechanically compatible: tests/_cdp.py:411-412 picks a free debug port and a mkdtemp profile per run, both passes share the static server on 8777, and the progress and out files are already separate (tools/ship.sh:877/881 and 938/939). builder_items.title: Do not batch 921 S3 pairings with checks run after Promise.all
builder_items.what: If this test is sped up, each pairing's readyState check and bulk send must run in that pairing's own continuation, right after its `opened` resolves. Checking the whole batch after Promise.all lets late pairs' bulk channels finish opening, which hides the 1-in-10 race the test exists to catch. Prove it with a mutation: make `opened` resolve on ctl only, and the test must still go red.

builder_items.title: Parallel ship passes conflict with the existing no-two-suites rule
builder_items.what: Running the 1280 and 380 passes at once is exactly the setup that flaked test 699 and cost a ship. That is why ship.sh refuses to run beside a spot-check. If it is tried anyway, ship.sh needs: a two-value phase, cancelling the other pass on red or timeout, not recording a contended pass into .suite-seconds, and staggered starts so _cdp.py's start-up reaper cannot kill the other run's Chrome or delete its profile. First do a trial on the 7.7 GB WSL laptop, outside a ship, logging memory, swap and flaky timing tests.

builder_items.title: The 'every tile' thumbnail seam is the real big win, larger than the report says
builder_items.what: The test's assertions (no stack growth, pick registers, swept >= 40, preview list, Done adds) don't depend on thumbnails, so skipping thumbnail rendering for this test keeps the proof. (2) The #1000 step 2 says to "compute _stale before notePending", but _stale is only set inside writeScene. (3) The #1002 text calls _sanitizeLayers the every-open load path. claims.evidence: js/storage.js:747 writeScene() returns false with _writeFail='stale' (:111, :115), but save() never checks it. The loop at :768-800 runs unconditionally, and :790 writes whenever existing.rev !== job.rev, so disk rev 1 gets overwritten by the stale tab's rev 0 job (planBlobWrites :572). idbPut's only scene-blob caller is :796. warnStale toast :89 claims nothing was saved over his work.

claims.claim: #1000 build step 2: stop notePending for a stale tab by computing _stale before it (:745)
claims.evidence: notePending (:599-612) runs before writeScene, and _stale only becomes true inside writeScene (:115). On the FIRST stale save the flag is still false, so checking _stale first does not catch it. The stale job (r:0) then overwrites the newer tab's note (r:1) because had.r !== j.rev (:606).
claims.correction: Call notePending right AFTER writeScene and skip it when _writeFail === 'stale'. Both calls are synchronous with no await between them, so the 'noted in the same tick as the document' guarantee in the comment at :740-742 still holds.

claims.claim: #1001: importObject creates the project before applyScene; a throw or a false return leaves an empty current project
claims.evidence: js/storage.js:1993-1999 creates and opens the project; :2000 awaits applyScene. The false branch at :2001-2005 only toasts and does not undo the create. A throw escapes to importFile's catch (:2027, toast 'Could not read that project file') or to restoreBackup's catch (:1951), which leaves one empty card per failed entry.

claims.evidence: storage.js is strict (:8). :1537 tests only truthiness and :1542 assigns .angle onto it, which throws for a string, number or true. sceneFileProblem (:1974-1981) never looks at layer fields. applyScene :1698 calls sanitizeImportedLayers, which reaches sanitizeUnsafeValues at :1647, after create. claims.claim: #1002: FM.storage._sanitizeLayers is the every-open load path

The every-open load is storage.js:903, which calls sanitizeUnsafeValues directly. That path throws too, so the fix location is still right.

summary: The bug diagnoses hold up. I traced all three lose-work bugs (#1004, #1005, #1006) in js/storage.js and each is reachable as described. The #1007 and #1008 code locations are also right. The fixes need corrections before anyone builds them. (1) #1004 says to copy the corrupt doc to `fm.proj.<id>.unreadable`. That name starts with the `fm.proj.` prefix, which five scanners treat as a project doc. The #1005 fix would then see the copy as an unreadable doc and stop the boot cleanup forever, even after he deletes the broken project, because remove() never deletes the copy. (2) #1004 step 2 says open() should return false once load() fails. Every caller reads false as "he chose to stay, nothing was torn down", but by then the previous project has already been closed. (3) #1007 only covers importFile, while Settings → Restore from a backup reads the whole file the same way, and backups are meant to be the big files. All five REQUESTS entries are JUMPED to ChatGPT ("land it, don't rebuild it"), so these plans are a checklist for reviewing ChatGPT's commits, not a build order. The container measurements (85 MB in 0.5 s, 13.1 ms at 250 groups) need a run I was not allowed to do.

builder_items.title: A corrupt project doc gets overwritten with a blank scene

When reviewing ChatGPT's fix: load() must unbind the tab on unparseable text, and open() must refuse BEFORE tearing anything down, because callers read false as 'nothing changed'.

builder_items.what: The proposed backup key fm.proj.<id>.unreadable (from VERIFIED.md and this plan) would be read as a project doc by every fm.proj.* scanner. Under the #1005 fail-closed rule it would stop the boot cleanup forever, and projects.remove() would never delete it. Use a key outside the prefix and remove it along with the project.

It also runs from every autosave, at most once every 12 s when nothing is playing (save :752 calls touchCurrent :2468). FX_MAX is cut at :1514 inside sanitizeEffects, which runs on every open (:903, :1779) and every undo (history.js:71), so lowering it would delete saved effects. Keeping 120 is right. It does not: an ordinary open runs only sanitizeMasks, sanitizeEffects and sanitizeUnsafeValues. sanitizeImportedLayers (keyframes, and wherever the text and path caps would go) runs on import, on templates, elements and friends' edits, and on EVERY UNDO. A keyframe or point cap there would therefore cut an existing project on the first undo of anything, and the autosave would then keep the cut version. That is the same data-loss shape as queue 680. (2) It says 'the sanitisers whitelist known keys' and proposes the Simple branch's smKeepUnknown rule for layers. Layers have no key whitelist today, so unknown top-level fields already survive. smKeepUnknown only applies inside `sm`. Using its limits (strings up to 200 characters, values up to 2 KB) on layers would start DROPPING plain fields that survive today, which breaks the very rule it quotes. Its 'futureField is kept' test would also pass on v17.23, so it cannot fail first. The pixel-parity claim for Fix 0 still needs a run: none of the scenes compared had a photo or video. Those are exactly what the halving loop was written for (the comment at :2130-2132 calls the old cards 'mushy'), and the compositor sets imageSmoothingQuality in only 2 places. The timing numbers (8.4 s vs 108 ms) and the 0.35-3.7 pixel differences were not re-run (not allowed here).

The skeleton is mostly right. The six touch points do exist roughly where the report says: FM.EFFECTS at compositor.js:50-1647, POSTFX at :3741, the three kernel tables at :5174, :10521 and :12534, CATEGORY_OF with a 'stylize' fallback at fx-registry.js:571/626, and the schema fingerprint at collab-core.js:243. claims.claim: Auto In/Out progress computed from t, layer.start and layer.duration in one trProgress helper makes all five transitions work with no keyframes
claims.evidence: A flattened group's proxy has tmp.start = t - 1 and tmp.duration = 2 (compositor.js:18519). Its real clock is _clipStart and _clipDuration (:18520-18521). Existing effects read those: motion blur at :3645-3648, and flashdark's fdLen at :7633, which also walks the splitOf lineage at :7635. With dur 0.5 on a group, pIn = clamp(1 - 1/0.5) = 0 and pOut = 0, so the transition never shows. With dur over 1 it sticks part-way. A split also copies effects, so an In and Out pair would fire at the cut unless lineage is handled.
claims.correction: trProgress must use start = layer._clipStart ?? layer.start and len = layer._clipDuration ?? layer.duration, and decide what a split half does (follow the splitOf lineage as flashdark does).

claims.claim: Confetti palette on Particles is byte-identical when absent (absent reads as 0, today's path untouched), and uses pHash(i*4+3) for the colour

But pHash(i*4+3) already sets each particle's rotation phase (compositor.js:14423), so colour would be tied to rotation. Slots 0-3 are all in use (:14388, :14396, :14397, :14423). The shape is clamped with Math.round(rd('shape', 0, 0, 4)) (:14359), so an appended heart (5) would render as Streak. Adding a param changes SCHEMA_FP, so a REV bump is required. builder_items.title: Auto transitions must read the group/split clock, not layer.start/duration
builder_items.what: If trProgress is built as specified, every auto In/Out transition on a group is dead or stuck part-way. The group proxy's start is t-1 and its duration is 2. Use _clipStart and _clipDuration, falling back to start and duration, and decide how split halves behave. flashdark follows the splitOf lineage.

builder_items.title: Transform-style transitions must draw through moverSource
builder_items.what: Zoom, Whip pan and Spin move the layer, so they must take their source from moverSource with their matrices, as spin, swing and shake do. Otherwise a clip scaled past the frame shows cut-off edges (the #986 C27 bug).

builder_items.title: Colour wheels with no-op defaults fails the 482 default-visibility test
builder_items.what: Every PIXEL_FX effect must change pixels visibly at its defaults. All-zero wheel amounts would turn the suite red and block the ship. Ship a visible default look.

builder_items.title: Particles palette: use a fresh hash slot and widen the shape clamp
builder_items.what: pHash(i*4+3) already drives each particle's rotation phase, so colour would correlate with rotation. Shape is clamped to 0..4, so an appended heart (5) would draw as a Streak.

builder_items.title: Collab fingerprint ignores a segment's options list
builder_items.what: SCHEMA_FP hashes key, type, default, legacy, min, max and keyframable, but not options. The sanitiser drops any segment value not in the options list. So two builds differing only by an appended option (such as a heart shape) would join one session, and the older one would strip the newer one's choice. Add the options to the hashed tuple, or bump REV by hand whenever an option is appended.

builder_items.title: Glitch cut duplicates the existing Glitch
builder_items.what: The existing Glitch already has Slices (default 14), an RGB tear, Amount and Re-roll. A short envelope as an EFFECT_PRESETS entry (like 'Glitch Pop') gives the same thing without a new type and without a fingerprint bump.
